about: workflow:keep-how-much-each-way-of-matching-is-worth: how much each way of matching (a search lane, or one model space in one place) is worth to this person, learned from what they open or use after a search, kept in the person's own store. It replaces the store half of tools/learn-how-much-each-way-of-matching-is-worth (src/search-answers.mjs, whose whole job was keeping the asked searches, the files they showed and the lane weights in the person's SQL store, and reading them back). The rule that a search is credited once, to the newest unanswered search that showed the used file, is the store's own key and sort (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do).

payload.label: Keep how much each way of matching is worth
payload.job: Keep, in the person's own store, each search asked (its lanes that took part, the time, and the files it showed with each lane's rank for them), credit a lane with the reciprocal of the rank when a file that search showed is used within the window (each search credited at most once, to the newest unanswered one), and read each lane's weight: the prior, pulled toward its answers, with a lane retired only after enough answers with its weight under the floor.
payload.produces: The store's own search, file and lane-weight objects, proven on the example attempts in PostgreSQL (PGlite) and a folder of JSON files: every search kept, every use credited or not, and every weight, retirement check and forget equal to the answers of the old module, which ran in SQLite.

source.from: tools/learn-how-much-each-way-of-matching-is-worth/src/search-answers.mjs at trillion-workshop origin/main 14c80bcd6 (the older repository's copy of the same file)
source.note: The constants are the person's search settings (fusion: followed_within_seconds, prior_answers, prior_reciprocal_rank, retire_after, retire_below); none is a default of this recipe. A search is kept with its time; asking a search again replaces it and makes it the newest. A search older than the window cannot be credited: each new search lets at most 8 of the expired searches go, with their files. A file used credits the newest unanswered search within the window that showed it, and only that one: every lane that took part gets 1 more answer and its reciprocal rank (0 when the lane did not rank the file). A weight is ((reciprocal + prior_answers x prior_reciprocal_rank) / (answers + prior_answers)) / prior_reciprocal_rank, and 1 for a lane with no answers. A lane in a prefix is retired only when there is at least one measured lane under the prefix, every one has at least retire_after answers, and each has a weight under retire_below. Forgetting a prefix deletes its lanes' weights, so the lane starts fresh when it is installed again. Nothing here names a lane, a model or a kind: lanes are the ids the search hands in.

where.description: Where the person keeps these things: the store's own address

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses, when it needs one

place.description: Where in the store these are kept, when they already are

fusion.description: The person's search settings: followed_within_seconds, prior_answers, prior_reciprocal_rank, retire_after, retire_below

operations.description: Each operation: asked (search, lanes, ranked as [{identity, ranks}], at), used (identity, at), weights (lanes), retired (prefix), forget (prefix)

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit where these are already kept (kept_in, or null) and the names of the objects that already keep them, and show them.

steps.title: Make the store's own objects, once
steps.do: When the look step found nothing, make the store's own objects in its own form: a search object keyed by its search id (its time, the lanes that took part, and whether it has been answered), a file-in-search object keyed by the file identity and the search id (the ranks by lane), and a lane-weight object keyed by the lane (its answers and the sum of its reciprocal ranks). Keep the newest-first order of a search's rows by its time and then by the order it was kept in. Submit the objects made.

steps.title: Prove the objects on the example attempts
steps.do: In a throwaway place in the same store, with the same objects and with the fusion settings {followed_within_seconds 600, prior_answers 2, prior_reciprocal_rank 0.5, retire_after 2, retire_below 0.2}, run these attempts in order, each at its time (seconds after 2026-11-18T12:00:00Z): [{"at": 0, "op": "asked", "search": "s1", "lanes": ["lane-a", "lane-b"], "ranked": [{"identity": "1f:aaa", "ranks": {"lane-a": 1, "lane-b": 3}}, {"identity": "1f:bbb", "ranks": {"lane-a": 2}}]}, {"at": 60, "op": "used", "identity": "1f:aaa"}, {"at": 70, "op": "used", "identity": "1f:aaa"}, {"at": 100, "op": "asked", "search": "s2", "lanes": ["lane-a"], "ranked": [{"identity": "1f:ccc", "ranks": {"lane-a": 1}}]}, {"at": 120, "op": "used", "identity": "1f:bbb"}, {"at": 130, "op": "used", "identity": "1f:ccc"}, {"at": 1000, "op": "asked", "search": "s3", "lanes": ["lane-c"], "ranked": [{"identity": "1f:ddd", "ranks": {"lane-c": 4}}]}, {"at": 1010, "op": "used", "identity": "1f:ddd"}, {"at": 1015, "op": "weights", "lanes": ["lane-a", "lane-b", "lane-c", "lane-z"]}, {"at": 1016, "op": "retired", "prefix": "lane-"}, {"at": 1020, "op": "used", "identity": "1f:zzz"}, {"at": 1030, "op": "forget", "prefix": "lane-c"}, {"at": 1031, "op": "weights", "lanes": ["lane-c"]}]. Submit outcomes (one per attempt: kept for asked, credited or not_credited for used, answered for weights and retired, forgotten for forget) and the answer: the weights at 1015, the retirement check at 1016, the used answer at 1020 and the weights at 1031.

checks.says: Each attempt is kept, credited, not credited, answered or forgotten as the intent says
The store's own objects give every expected answer

steps.title: Keep this run's operations
steps.do: Run each operation in order through the store's own objects: asked keeps the search (replacing one of the same id, which makes it the newest) and its files, then lets at most 8 expired searches and their files go; used credits the newest unanswered search within the window that showed the file, once, and marks it answered, or answers false; weights reads each lane's weight from the store and the prior; retired answers whether every measured lane under the prefix is retired; forget deletes the lanes under the prefix. Submit results (one per operation, the answer it gave) and kept_records (each search and file kept), and found_records (each search read back). With no operations, submit empty lists.

checks.says: Every search read back was kept

payload.erase: On the person's request the store deletes the searches, files and lane weights it holds (all of them, or the ones under a prefix); nothing keeps a copy outside the store.
